name: Jaipur Foot prosthesis and access
description: Ram Chandra Sharma and Pramod Karan Sethi developed the Jaipur Foot prosthesis in India in 1968.

impact.note: A cheap, locally suited version of an existing prosthesis served amputees in India and other poor countries, with a few later variants.

date.basis: Date applies to this specific event or witness, not global invention.

events.statement: Ram Chandra Sharma and Pramod Karan Sethi developed the Jaipur Foot prosthesis in India in 1968.

evidence.locator: Jaipur Foot and intraocular lenses, pp. 54–56
evidence.supports: WHO dates Jaipur Foot development to 1968, reports free provision under BMVSS from 1975 and 59 limbs fitted in its first year. It reports Aurolab producing nearly 35,000 lenses in 1992 at roughly US$10 each. The counts are not patient counts and the cost is not necessarily a patient charge; a separate overview states US$5 on an unclear basis.

events.caveats: The WHO account is retrospective and other accounts give 1969. Manufacture cost is not treated as a patient charge; access counts are specific to the named service.
